newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Premiere debuts at 1.10 peso.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Premiere debuts at 1.10 peso.

text.p: The Philippines' Premiere Entertainment Production Inc made its debut on Monday at 1.10 peso, compared with an offering price of one peso.
Premiere, the first movie production company to list on the Philippine Stock Exchange, is offering 180 million common shares or 34.62 percent of the company.
Brokers said Premiere had traded on the grey market as high as 1.30 pesos the week immediately after the start of its IPO last April 2.

Premiere's listing came at a time when the stock market has been reeling from poor first quarter corporate earnings, fears of a property glut and its effect on banking sector as well as negative sentiment towards the region.
After the opening bell, the stock traded as high as 1.16 pesos. At 0145 GMT, it was the second most heavily traded issue with volume reaching 24.26 million shares.
The company has projected a 17.39 million peso net income this year against a net loss of 14.42 million last year after it produced four movies, two of which were flops.
Proceeds of the IPO will be used partly to cover the production of films and television shows and the acquisition of production and film equipment.
